title: Fit a new 300 mm etch-chamber edge ring, clocked by eye to its locating pins, without touching the chuck
instruction: Install the new edge ring from the stand in the etch chamber, seated on its locating pins, and take your hands out of the chamber.
context: Plasma etch chambers, which cut the patterns into every AI chip, have a consumable edge ring around the wafer chuck (here single-crystal silicon). The plasma erodes it, so it is replaced at chamber maintenance. On cathodes with edge-ring lift pins the pins raise the ring to an exchange position and lower it onto three locating dowels; here the robot does the hand-off at that position, lid open, old ring already out (lowering the pins first and setting the ring straight onto the dowels also counts). The new ring is 360 mm across, 4 mm thick and brittle; it lies on its stand at a different angle each trial and fits the dowels at one angle only. The cue is visual: the white dowels show through the ring's three slots. It must come down with every dowel within about 0.35 mm of its slot's centre; further off it can jam on a dowel's lead-in or land on the tips. Touching the chuck face, dropping the ring, pressing it onto a pin or leaving it on the dowel tips scraps parts.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. (1) Replica of a 300 mm etch chamber's lower body with the lid and upper chamber removed, cathode axis at x 40.5, y 0: anodised aluminium bowl, bore 46 cm, continuous rim 12.7 cm above the ring seat, seat 2.9 cm above the table. In it, from the centre out: the electrostatic chuck (alumina puck, 298 mm diameter, face 2.5 mm above the seat; keep it clean); the quartz base ring (bore 298.6 mm, outer 380 mm, top = the seat) with three white alumina locating dowels (4.0 mm diameter, 3.8 mm proud, 0.8 mm x 45 deg tip chamfer) on a 320 mm circle at 0, 115 and 245 degrees anticlockwise from +x (top view); three sapphire lift pins (3 mm, flat tips) on a 340 mm circle at 60, 180 and 300 degrees, raised 25 mm above the seat (maintenance position); the installed quartz cover ring (bore 362 mm, outer 420 mm, top 4 mm above the seat). (2) Maintenance pendant on the table at x 30, y -36 (9 x 6 x 4 cm, dark grey) with two 20 mm keys on top: blue RING UP (nearer the robot) and orange RING DOWN (farther); a key acts when pressed with about 5 N for 0.1 s and moves the lift pins at 5 mm/s (25 mm up or 1 mm below the seat). (3) New edge ring: single-crystal silicon, outer 360 mm, bore 299 mm, 4.0 mm thick, 0.29 kg, three radial through-slots 4.3 x 8 mm (0.15 mm play a side on the dowels) on a 320 mm circle at 0, 115 and 245 degrees of the ring (the same pattern as the dowels). It lies on a ring stand at x 12.0, y 0: black Delrin post (40 mm) with three 15 mm wide arms at 45, 170 and 300 degrees (station frame, fixed) carrying the ring 17.0 cm above the table (just above the bowl wall), turned so that its slot pattern is offset from the chamber's dowels by a start angle drawn per trial uniformly from -25 to -10 or +10 to +22 deg (anticlockwise positive, top view; never within 10 deg of fitting), and the stand moved by up to 1 cm in x and y (both from the trial seed). Named check setups: -25, -20, -15, +15, +20 deg, stand not moved (real trials use these, from marks on the stand every 5 deg).
scoring: Read at the end of the trial (person check in brackets). 0 if at any time: anything touched the chuck face or edge (video; a wipe of the chuck shows marks), the ring was dropped or fell (more than 2 mm of free fall; video), the robot pressed the ring onto pins or chamber parts with more than its weight plus 10 N for 50 ms during hand contact (tared 1 kHz tri-axial support-force trace synchronized to video; fixture/assembly.md), or the ring rested on the dowel tips for 0.5 s or more (video: ring held up on the dowels, not seated; sim: the base ring with its dowels carries half its weight while its bottom is more than 0.8 mm above the seat). 0.5: seated as below but a hand still in the bowl or within 3 cm of the ring. 1.0 (ends the trial): the lift pins lowered and the ring seated flat on the base ring with all three dowels through its slots (a 0.1 mm feeler does not enter under the ring at any slot; sim: ring within 0.3 mm of the seat and 0.15 deg of level), both hands out of the bowl and 3 cm or more from the ring, ring still for 1 s. Otherwise 0: ring left on the stand or on the lift pins (however well placed: only seating shows the fit), or lowered onto the dowel tips.
reset_notes: Press RING UP, lift the ring off the raised pins by its edges (gloves), check it for chips at the slots, and lay it on the stand turned to the next setup's angle (marks on the stand arms every 5 deg). Check the chuck face is clean. Setups run in order 0-4.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena yam_arena, PhysX (CPU) 480 Hz, 20 Hz control. Ring set geometry is representative (OEM drawings are proprietary), full size. Ring: free rigid body of 131 convex pieces; chamber parts, stand and pendant are kinematic so contact forces can be read. Lift pins are a position-controlled device (5 mm/s), moved only by the keys. No welds, snaps or proximity rules. Friction 0.3 (silicon on quartz/alumina) and 0.5 (pads) are estimates. Full statement: README.
run_limit: 3000 control steps (2.5 min at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Scripted reference 1.0 in 1,001 control steps. Dream-1 (seed 0) scored 0.0 at the 3,000-step limit. Pressing the ring produced 27.08 N of support force for an excessive push lasting 1.27 s and scored 0.0.
